currentContext.expansion: Expansion is being executed almost entirely through the Company's three subsidiaries under a section headed 'Strategic Initiatives, Expansion and Capital Expenditure'. Backward integration for key steering-gear components through DriveSys Systems Private Limited (wholly owned, MIDC Supa, Parner, Ahilyanagar) has been successfully implemented and is operational, supplying housings, sector shafts, pistons, oil tanks, plastic mouldings and steering pump assemblies primarily to the Company, with external-market opportunities being explored after internal demand is met. On top of that, a diversification strategy is underway into SG Iron castings, Aluminium Extrusion and Electrical Equipment Components. DriveSys is building an Aluminium Division (melting, extrusion, machining, fabrication) at MIDC Supa with a project cost of about Rs. 100 crore; it is described as nearing completion with Rs. 90 crore of capital expenditure incurred to date, DriveSys having executed a Lease Deed with MIDC and acquired leasehold rights to an industrial plot and factory building transferred from NexSteer, and a December 2025 order for machined aluminium parts of approximately Rs. 151 crore is to be delivered over 15 months. DriveSys is also building an Electrical Division for MCB/MCCB, RCB and Mechanism Operated Auxiliary Contactors at MIDC Nagapur, Ahilyanagar, where two adjacent premises were taken on sub-lease in January 2026; project cost is about Rs. 12 crore, Rs. 9.2 crore has been incurred, civil works and plant installation are substantially progressed, trial runs have commenced and commercial production is expected shortly subject to stabilisation, PPAP and statutory approvals. Metacast Auto Private Limited, a 51% subsidiary and foundry joint venture with Supreme Iron (India) Private Limited that acts as Captive Process Vendor to DriveSys, began commercial production in November 2024, reached record utilisation in March 2026, and proposes to raise casting capacity from 10,000 to 25,000 metric tonnes per annum by installing one additional production line, with a fresh investment of Rs. 25 crore funded mainly through borrowings. NexSteer Systems Private Limited has not commenced business operations and transferred its MIDC leasehold rights and building to DriveSys during the year. For its own plants, the Company states it has planned Rs. 35 crore in the current financial year towards replacement of old machinery and balancing equipment at the Pune and Pithampur factories, and has allocated around Rs. 88 crore towards subsidiaries of which Rs. 25 crore is for expansion of their existing business. On financing, the Company says it is evaluating options to meet subsidiary capital expenditure - currently funded primarily by loans from the holding company - and is exploring strengthening the subsidiaries' capital structure through equity infusion and optimisation of the debt-equity mix, subject to detailed evaluation and requisite approvals.
